doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Audition by fire: reading Basie's book at Disneyland
summary: He read chord charts but not notes; at his first Disneyland date Al Grey and others called numbers while Basie doodled, and Heard passed because he knew the music.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well that’s interesting. When you get the bass book for Count Basie, what does it look like? Is it chord charts? Is it, you know — or did you learn by listening to the band?
Actually I could read from the chord charts. But reading notes and things like that I wasn’t very good at.
But how did you catch all the kicks?

When I first joined, and this is the truth, you can ask Al Grey about this, right? He was here earlier, you can ask him about this. When I first joined the band at Disneyland, I showed up and they had this book there, and I’m acting like I knew what I was doing, then so the band hits, Count Basie’s like doodling as he always did, and by the way, they could tell what was coming up by the way he was doodling. So it’d be new. So I asked Al Grey, “What number?” Al say, “2-4-81” and another guy said, “5-90” and another guy said, “17.” In the meantime Basie’s doodling, so the band finally goes into this thing and I played it ‘cause I knew the music. And that’s what they wanted to know if I could do anyway.
So that was your audition almost? Trial by fire, huh?
